concepts.def: Whole number with no fractional part, positive, negative or zero (e.g., 7, -42, 0).
Number with a fractional part stored using floating-point representation (e.g., 3.14).
Data type with only two possible values: True or False, used for logical conditions.
Single letter, digit or symbol, typically stored using ASCII or Unicode codes.
Ordered sequence of characters, used to store text such as names or sentences.
Converting a value from one data type to another, e.g., int("5") gives integer 5.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Data Transmission & Networking — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Data Transmission & Networking brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Data Transmission & Networking.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
